subject.title: ACP parent session stuck until refresh when yielded waiting for child completion

question: Should OpenClaw implement one dedicated yielded-parent wake/resume contract across ACP terminal tasks, native subagent announces, blocked/give-up delivery, and heartbeat-disabled deployments, or continue landing per-runtime wake slices?
rationale: The source and related PRs show multiple plausible repair seams, but choosing the permanent owner boundary affects session state, message delivery, heartbeat semantics, and future compatibility.

options.title: Converge on a cross-runtime contract
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and require candidate PRs to fit one maintainer-approved yielded-parent wake/resume design across ACP and native subagents.

options.title: Land narrow slices independently
options.body: Allow PRs such as the ACP terminal-task and blocked-delivery fixes to land as incremental mitigations while tracking remaining gaps separately.

options.title: Defer until live proof narrows it
options.body: Hold architectural changes until a maintainer-sponsored live repro isolates which wake path should own the full fix.

recommendation.title: Converge on a cross-runtime contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and require candidate PRs to fit one maintainer-approved yielded-parent wake/resume design across ACP and native subagents.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest current-main involvement in subagent completion handoff and active parent wake paths.
